$comment: Single catalog of aquila-react-ai quality rules, aligned with the Sonar way profile. Each rule is a principle + the Sonar rule (common anchor) + the local ESLint enforcement when one exists. Levels: standard ⊂ high. Read with `npx aquila-react-ai lint rules`.

rules.title: No explicit `any`/dynamic type
rules.why: An explicit type is the contract the compiler and the AI check; `any` hides errors.

rules.title: Every promise is awaited or handled
rules.why: A dangling promise loses errors and breaks transaction ordering.

rules.title: `async` only when there is an `await`; `return await` inside try/catch
rules.why: Without await the function need not be async; outside try the extra await only costs.

rules.title: No unused variables/parameters (`_` prefix to ignore on purpose)
rules.why: Dead code confuses readers and the AI that copies the pattern.

rules.title: No `console` in `src`: use the project logger / error reporter (e.g. Sentry) or remove it
rules.why: Browser consoles leak data to anyone with devtools; only the logger/reporter carries level, context and redaction.

rules.title: No `debugger` statements in code
rules.why: It halts execution in production.

rules.title: Strict equality (`===`/`!==`)
rules.why: Implicit coercion causes hard-to-spot bugs.

rules.title: `{}` blocks on every `if`/`for`/`while`
rules.why: Avoids the classic bug of the second line outside the block.

rules.title: No nested ternaries
rules.why: Unreadable; use if/else or a function.

rules.title: Cognitive complexity per function ≤ 15
rules.why: Above this the function does too much: extract named steps.

rules.title: No converting objects to string without a format (`String(obj)`, `${obj}` → "[object Object]")
rules.why: Logs and messages become useless; use a helper that serializes.

rules.title: Optional chaining instead of `&&` chains
rules.why: Shorter and no false negatives with 0/''.

rules.title: No unnecessary type assertions
rules.why: Casts that do not change the type hide the real reasoning.

rules.title: Environment variables only in configuration modules
rules.why: `process.env`/`import.meta.env` are read and validated in one typed config module (e.g. `src/config/env.ts` with Zod); the rest imports it (allowed paths: `lint.options.configPaths`).

rules.title: Every test has at least one explicit assert
rules.why: A test without an assert always passes; in e2e keep the response and `expect(...)` on it.

rules.title: No focused or disabled tests (`only`/`skip`/`x`)
rules.why: They hide suite failures in CI.

rules.title: Rules of Hooks: hooks only at the top level of components and custom hooks
rules.why: A conditional or looped hook breaks React's call-order bookkeeping and corrupts state.

rules.title: Effect/memo/callback dependency arrays are complete
rules.why: A missing dependency is a stale closure: the effect reads old props/state. Fix the code, never silence the rule.

rules.title: Every element rendered from a list has a `key`
rules.why: Without a key React reuses the wrong DOM/state between renders.

rules.title: No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (sanitize with DOMPurify and justify the exception inline)
rules.why: It bypasses React's escaping: the classic XSS hole.

rules.title: Accessibility basics: `alt` on images, real links/buttons, labels on form controls, keyboard for click handlers
rules.why: Users with screen readers or keyboards must be able to use the UI; also what RTL `getByRole` queries rely on.

rules.title: Type-only imports use `import type`
rules.why: Separates runtime dependencies from compile-time ones.

rules.title: No type annotations the compiler already infers; no unnecessary `=== true`
rules.why: Noise that adds no contract.

rules.title: Members never reassigned are `readonly`
rules.why: Explicit immutability; the AI does not introduce accidental mutations.

rules.title: No unnecessary ternaries (`x ? x : y` → `x ?? y`; `c ? true : false` → `c`)
rules.why: Shorter idiomatic form.

rules.title: No negated conditions with `else` (swap the branches)
rules.why: Read the positive case first.

rules.title: Built-in modules with protocol (`node:fs`)
rules.why: Distinguishes built-ins from packages.

rules.title: Modern APIs: `replaceAll`, `.at(-1)`, `.some()`, `Set#has`, `Object.hasOwn`, `??=`/`||=`
rules.why: Parity with Sonar; explicit intent.

rules.title: No redundant spreads/push and re-exports via `export … from`
rules.why: Fewer copies and fewer lines.

rules.title: No duplicate or redundant union members
rules.why: `string | 'a'` is just `string`.

rules.title: Type errors throw `TypeError`
rules.why: Correct error class for type validation.

rules.title: SonarJS recommended profile (Sonar bugs and code smells in the editor)
rules.why: Anticipates the Sonar quality gate; noisy rules turned off.

rules.title: Functions and components ≤ 80 lines, ≤ 5 parameters (constructors excluded), nesting ≤ 3
rules.why: Small functions are testable and fit in the AI context.

rules.title: Specific asserts (`toHaveLength`, not `.length).toBe`)
rules.why: Useful failure message.

rules.title: Test titles in present tense, no "should" (and no ticket ids: lint.options.ticketPattern)
rules.why: They describe the behavior, not the task.

rules.title: No array index as `key`
rules.why: Index keys mix up state when items are inserted, removed or reordered; use a stable id.

rules.title: No component defined inside another component
rules.why: A new component type every render remounts the subtree and loses its state.

rules.title: No trivial asserts (that always pass) and no duplicate cases in `it.each`
rules.why: Only asserts that can fail count (Sonar S5914/S5976; no local rule — review).

rules.title: Clone dates with `new Date(d.getTime())`
rules.why: Sonar parity (no local rule — review).
